name: Sellat Proof for WooCommerce
author: skanthemore

sections.description:
When a customer says they never accepted your terms, or disputes what they ordered and when, a screenshot of your admin is your word against theirs. Sellat Proof for WooCommerce keeps independent, timestamped evidence of both, from the moment the order is confirmed.

What it records

  • Every confirmed order, paid or on hold waiting for a bank transfer. The order number, dates, amounts, products, status and payment method, the version of your terms and privacy policy in force at checkout, and a fingerprint of the customer’s email. This proof record never includes the customer’s name, address, email or phone.
  • Every version of your legal pages. Terms and conditions, privacy policy, returns and shipping. Each time the content of one changes, a new version is recorded with its exact text, and each order points to the version in force when it was placed.

How it is protected

The record is sent to Sellat, which anchors its fingerprint on public blockchains (Polygon and Bitcoin). Nothing personal is published: only a hash.

  • Free daily protection. The day’s orders are grouped into one proof of your shop, anchored once a day. Each order keeps its record and its path in the day’s tree. Any order you choose can also get an eIDAS qualified timestamp by hand, with its own proof, spending one of your account’s seals.

Verifiable without Sellat

From each order you can download a proof pack: the record, the exact text of the accepted terms, the public proof on the blockchains and a README that explains how to check everything with standard tools. Once downloaded, a pack checks without Sellat. Your shop also keeps its own copy of every record and, once each proof is final, of the proof itself (the day’s tree and anchor, an order’s own proof and seal, each legal version’s proof): if Sellat cannot be reached, the plugin builds the same pack from those copies.

Built for WooCommerce

  • Classic checkout and the Cart and Checkout blocks.
  • High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).
  • Background jobs with Action Scheduler: the checkout never waits for Sellat. If Sellat cannot be reached, orders wait and are sent later, with retries.
  • A Usage screen: everything protected in the last 7, 30 or 90 days, sales covered, eIDAS seals issued and left, a chart per day, and what your plan has left.
  • A Sellat box on each order, a Sellat column in the orders list, and WooCommerce → Sellat with the connection, the protection settings, the orders, the legal pages and a log of every call.
  • The API key is stored encrypted. Personal data tools: the acceptance IP joins WooCommerce’s export and erasure, and a suggested text is added to Settings → Privacy.

More about the plugin, and a sample of the certificate it gives each legal page version: sellat.app/en/woocommerce.

Please note: this plugin helps you keep evidence. It does not by itself make your shop compliant with any law, and whether a proof is accepted, and with what weight, is for the court or authority that sees it to decide.

External services

This plugin connects to Sellat (https://sellat.app), the service that records and timestamps the proofs. Nothing is sent until you connect your shop in WooCommerce → Sellat, either by signing in to Sellat from there or by pasting an API key.

Once connected, the plugin sends to Sellat’s API (https://sellat.app/api/v2):

  • When you click “Connect with Sellat”: your browser opens sellat.app with your shop’s random identifier, its domain, the address to come back to and your WordPress language, so the page opens in it.
  • When you connect, and when you test the connection: your shop’s domain, its name, its random identifier, and the versions of WordPress, WooCommerce, PHP and the plugin.
  • To show what your plan allows: your plan, seals and limits are read from Sellat when you open the plugin’s screens (at most every 5 minutes) and once a day.
  • When you connect and when you save your protection settings (and later, if Sellat could not be reached): your protection settings (how orders are proven, the eIDAS seal and whether the acceptance IP is included), which Sellat checks against your plan.
  • When a legal page changes: the fingerprint (SHA-256) of the page’s content, its URL, type, language and version number, and the text of the page itself, so that every proof pack can carry the exact terms. Once a day the plugin checks the pages for changes and asks Sellat for the state of their proofs.
  • When an order is confirmed (paid, or on hold waiting for an offline payment such as a bank transfer): the order record: its number, dates, amounts, products, status, payment method and language; the customer’s account number, if they have one, and the fingerprint of their email; the version and address of the terms they accepted and of the privacy policy shown at checkout; and your shop’s name, domain and, if you enter it, tax ID. It includes the acceptance IP only if you turn that option on.
  • Only if your Sellat account includes custody and you turn it on: a full copy of the order, including the customer’s name, addresses, email and phone. Until Sellat keeps it, the copy waits on your server encrypted; a server that cannot encrypt it (PHP without OpenSSL) neither keeps nor sends it.
  • When you download a proof pack: the order’s billing email, so that Sellat can check it against the fingerprint in the record and include it in the pack. Sellat does not keep it.
  • When you ask for it from an order or a legal version: an eIDAS qualified timestamp, a certificate or a pack, or removing a copy from custody.
  • To keep states up to date: requests for the state of your orders, every 15 minutes while some are not final, and the address where Sellat can notify your shop (only for shops served over https). When you delete the plugin, it asks Sellat to stop those notifications.

Sellat anchors fingerprints on Polygon and on Bitcoin (through OpenTimestamps), and requests eIDAS qualified timestamps from a qualified trust service provider. The plugin itself never contacts them.

Sellat’s terms and conditions and privacy policy.

The plugin also makes one request to your own site: when a legal page changes, it fetches the page as a visitor sees it and keeps that copy as context, in your uploads folder.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “Sellat Proof for WooCommerce”, install and activate it. WooCommerce must be active.
  2. Go to WooCommerce → Sellat and click “Connect with Sellat”. You sign in to Sellat (or create a free account), confirm, and you come back connected. If you integrate by hand, you can paste an API key instead.
  3. In the Protection tab, choose the legal pages the plugin should watch. Your WooCommerce terms page and your privacy policy page are chosen for you.

From then on, every confirmed order is recorded. Orders confirmed before you connect wait and are sent once you do.

Nothing else to set up. The plugin keeps its private copies in wp-content/uploads/sellat-proof/ and protects that folder itself: it cannot be listed, the order files have names that cannot be guessed, and the full order copies kept for custody (with the customer’s name and addresses) are encrypted. On Apache and LiteSpeed (most hosting) the .htaccess the plugin writes also closes it completely.

Optional, only for nginx servers you manage: this rule closes the folder completely there too. On managed hosting, you can ask your host’s support to add it.

location ~* /wp-content/uploads/sellat-proof/ { deny all; }
sections.faq:
Do I need a Sellat account?

Yes. The proofs are made by the Sellat service. The free account includes the daily protection of your orders, the recording of your legal pages and the eIDAS qualified timestamp by hand, paid with seal credits.

What does the eIDAS qualified timestamp cost?

It is optional. Each one uses a seal credit from your Sellat account: every account gets one free, and more are sold in packs. Nothing is spent unless you press “Add eIDAS seal” on an order and confirm. See Sellat’s prices.

What if my legal pages use shortcodes, blocks or a page builder?

Sellat records each legal page as WordPress renders it for a visitor, and “Local copy” in WooCommerce → Sellat → Legal pages opens each version exactly as it was recorded. Every WordPress is different: check that what is recorded is what your customers see. A shortcode, block or plugin that changes the page for each visitor, or hides part of it, may not have been foreseen. If something does not match, write to us at help@sellat.app.

Can someone recover my customer’s email from the record?

No. The record carries a fingerprint of the email, not the email. Whoever holds the record, though, can check whether a given email is the one in it: that is what lets anyone verify a proof pack, which carries the email.

What happens if Sellat is down?

Nothing at checkout: the plugin never makes the customer wait. The order is marked as waiting and is sent later, with retries, and the WooCommerce → Sellat → Log tab shows each attempt. Proofs that are already final do not need Sellat at all: your shop keeps a copy of each one and builds the proof pack from it.

What happens to my proofs if I delete the plugin?

They stay in Sellat, and by default the plugin leaves each order’s link to its proof and your local copies in place. Deleting the plugin forgets the API key and the settings. To remove everything, define SELLAT_PROOF_REMOVE_ALL_DATA as true in wp-config.php before deleting it.

Does it need the PHP mbstring extension?

No. Without it, the plugin lowercases only ASCII letters when it fingerprints the customer’s email, so an email with an accented letter would get a fingerprint different from the one Sellat computes; with mbstring (installed on nearly every host) they always match.

Does it work with the block checkout and with HPOS?

Yes, both.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Until the shop is connected, every screen of the plugin says so, with a button to connect it: nothing is protected before that.
  • Connecting is one button, “Connect with Sellat”; pasting an API key moves under “Integrating by hand?”.
  • Sellat’s connect and sign-in pages open in your WordPress language (Spanish, English, German or French).

1.0.0

  • First public release: daily proofs of confirmed orders, legal page versions, the eIDAS qualified timestamp by hand, proof packs (also built by the shop from its own copies of the final proofs), a Usage screen, block checkout and HPOS support.

screenshots.caption: The Sellat box on an order: the state of its proof and the proof pack, certificate and eIDAS seal.
Protection: the daily proof of your orders, the eIDAS seal by hand and the legal pages to watch.
Orders: every order with the state of its proof, filters and bulk actions.
Legal pages: every version of your legal pages with its fingerprint and its proof.
Connection: connect your shop to Sellat in one click.
Usage: what the shop protected in the period, day by day, and what the plan has left.
